title: Publish the Secondary School Coding Club & Inter-School Tech Tournament Blueprint, by Fri 18 Dec
description:
Inter-school coding leagues, hackathons, and high-school STEM clubs need safe, school-compliant digital venues for students aged 13–18. School administrators routinely block external tools like Discord due to unvetted adult exposure, data privacy concerns, and lack of teacher supervision. This blueprint establishes Zedu as the premier school-sanctioned, teacher-moderated tournament and club platform.

Work under this goal:
- Architect the inter-school tournament workspace structure: school-specific student squad channels (#school-kings-college, #school-queens-college), teacher supervisor control channels, and public tournament scoreboard channels.
- Author the 30-minute teacher-supervised lightning coding challenge protocol using native Zedu Buzz sessions with verified instructor host permissions.
- Design the project submission and peer showcase thread protocol in Zedu's 440px thread drawer with strict moderation rules.
- Draft the student participant consent and parent information pack distributed through Zedu File Management.

Done when: A comprehensive tournament operations kit is delivered with school safety configurations, teacher supervision workflows, student coding challenge templates, and verified zedu.chat channel permission settings.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Settle the age and consent position first, because the blueprint targets learners aged 13-18
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Before any workspace design, record what Zedu's current terms and privacy policy say about minimum age and parental consent, and what the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 requires for processing children's data. If the terms set a minimum age above 13, or say nothing, the blueprint must say that and route the decision to the team, not market a school-sanctioned venue for minors. Also note that the web app has no report-message or block-user control today. Done: an age and consent fact sheet with sources, the school consent letter template, and the conditions under which the tournament blueprint can be published.
